name: Claronite-XV
description: A transparent polycrystalline alumina-spinel ceramic manufactured via quantum-assisted hot isostatic pressing, achieving optical clarity comparable to borosilicate glass while exceeding diamond hardness on the Vickers scale. The quantum sintering process eliminates grain boundary scattering, producing a fully dense, pore-free matrix with near-zero birefringence. Originally developed for orbital observation domes, it has since become the prestige standard for armored visors and high-security glazing.
story_hooks: A Tier 1 fixer obtains a cracked Claronite-XV visor panel — even damaged, it's worth a year's wages, and multiple parties want it back.
A counterfeit Claronite-XV batch has been circulating in Tier 2 markets; it looks identical but shatters under ballistic impact, and someone is already dead.

An Apex Nanofabrication technician has discovered how to produce Claronite-XV with a secondary quantum sintering flaw that makes it selectively opaque to specific surveillance frequencies — corporate espionage or liberation tool?
